meta.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
meta.author: bank-team-web-development
meta.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.topic: The document as a tree rather than a typed sequence
questions.learningObjective: Identify the parent node of a selected element
questions.stem:
In a spreadsheet's markup
42
, how many element children does the div contain?

options.text: One, because only the table is a direct child of the div
Two, because the table and its row are both direct children of the div
options.misconception: counts nested descendants as direct children

options.text: Zero, because the div holds only text content
options.misconception: confuses element children with text nodes

options.text: Three, counting the td as a sibling of the table
options.misconception: misreads the nesting depth of the tree

questions.explanation: The div's direct element children are just the table; the tr and td are descendants nested inside it. Counting descendants as children overcounts the tree levels.
questions.hint: Count only nodes one level below the div.

questions.topic: A block element written inside a paragraph
questions.learningObjective: Predict how the browser splits a paragraph around a block child
questions.stem: In a spreadsheet's notes field, a p element contains a div; what does the browser do when parsing that markup?

options.text: It keeps the div inside the paragraph as an inline child
options.misconception: assumes paragraphs can contain any flow content

options.text: It discards the div entirely as invalid markup
options.misconception: thinks invalid children are dropped rather than reparented

options.text: It converts the div into a span automatically
options.misconception: imagines the parser rewrites tags to fit

questions.explanation: A paragraph cannot contain block-level flow content, so the parser implicitly closes the p before the div and reopens a new p afterward. The div becomes a sibling, not a child.
questions.hint: Block content inside a paragraph ends that paragraph.

questions.topic: Display decides block or inline, not the tag name
questions.learningObjective: Choose the property that controls box generation
questions.stem: A spreadsheet's status badge uses display:inline on a div to sit beside text; a teammate says the div tag itself forces a new line. What is the error?

options.text: The teammate thinks inline elements cannot contain block children
options.misconception: mixes display with content model rules

options.text: The teammate believes CSS cannot change an element's display
The teammate forgets that div is void and needs no closing tag
options.misconception: misremembers div as a void element

questions.explanation: Box generation follows the computed display value, not the tag name, so a div with display:inline flows inline. Tag defaults are only defaults and can be overridden.
questions.hint: Display, not the tag, decides the box.

questions.topic: Choosing an element for what it means rather than how it looks
questions.learningObjective: Select a semantic element over a styled generic one
questions.stem: In a spreadsheet app, a clickable summary should be marked up with the element that conveys its role rather than a styled div; give a model answer.

answer.exemplar: Use a button element for the clickable summary because it carries the correct role, keyboard support, and focus behavior, while a styled div would only mimic appearance and miss accessibility semantics.

questions.explanation: Semantic elements encode meaning and default behavior; choosing by appearance alone loses accessibility and structure. A button provides keyboard and focus handling for free.
questions.hint: Pick the element whose default role matches the action.

questions.topic: What a heading outline with a skipped level claims
questions.learningObjective: Recognize the effect of skipping a heading level
questions.stem: A spreadsheet report jumps from an h2 section title to an h4 subsection; what does the outline claim about that subsection?

options.text: The outline becomes invalid and browsers ignore all headings
options.misconception: overstates the consequence of a skipped level

options.text: The subsection belongs directly to the h2 with no intermediate level
options.misconception: treats the skipped level as simply absent

options.text: The subsection is a child of a missing h3 that does not exist
The h4 is promoted to an h3 automatically

questions.explanation: A skipped level implies an implied intermediate heading, so the h4 is treated as nested under a missing h3. The outline still parses but represents a nonexistent parent.
questions.hint: A gap implies a missing parent heading.

questions.topic: Heading levels are structure rather than size
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish heading semantics from visual size
questions.stem: In a spreadsheet dashboard, an h1 is styled small and an h3 is styled large; which statement about the outline is true?

options.text: The h3 becomes the top-level heading because it looks larger
options.misconception: equates visual size with outline rank

options.text: Both headings share the same outline rank after styling
CSS size overrides the heading level in the outline
The h1 remains the top-level heading regardless of styling

questions.explanation: Heading rank comes from the tag, not CSS size, so the h1 stays top-level even when rendered small. Visual styling does not rewrite the document outline.
questions.hint: Tag, not CSS, sets the rank.

questions.topic: What a form actually submits
questions.learningObjective: Name the data a form sends on submit
questions.stem: A spreadsheet's expense form has inputs named amount and category; what does it submit when the user presses submit?

options.text: The visible labels and placeholder text of each field
The CSS classes applied to each input element
The name and current value pairs of the successful controls
The entire HTML of the form element
options.misconception: imagines the whole markup is posted

questions.explanation: Forms submit successful controls as name-value pairs, not labels, classes, or markup. Only controls with names contribute to the payload.
questions.hint: Name-value pairs of successful controls.

questions.topic: Collapsing a run of white space in ordinary text
questions.learningObjective: Predict how whitespace collapses in normal flow
questions.stem: A spreadsheet note contains three spaces between two words; a reviewer expects three gaps in the rendered text. What is the error?

options.text: The reviewer assumes tabs render as eight spaces
options.misconception: confuses tab width with space collapsing

options.text: The reviewer thinks CSS always preserves every space
The reviewer believes spaces are converted to non-breaking spaces
The reviewer ignores that normal flow collapses whitespace runs

questions.explanation: In ordinary text, runs of spaces, tabs, and newlines collapse to a single space, so three spaces render as one gap. Whitespace preservation requires pre or white-space:pre.
questions.hint: Runs of whitespace collapse to one space.

questions.topic: The outer width under the initial box-sizing
questions.learningObjective: Compute outer width with default content-box
questions.stem: A spreadsheet column is set to width 200px with 20px padding and 2px border using the initial box-sizing; explain the rendered outer width.

answer.exemplar: With the initial content-box sizing, the declared 200px applies only to the content, so the outer width becomes 200 plus 40 padding plus 4 border, totaling 244 pixels.

questions.explanation: Under content-box, width covers only content; padding and border add to the total. Adding them gives the true outer width on screen.
questions.hint: Add padding and border to the content width.

questions.topic: The content width under border-box sizing
questions.learningObjective: Compute content width with border-box
questions.stem: A spreadsheet cell uses box-sizing:border-box with width 200px, 20px padding, and 2px border; what is the content width?

options.text: 200px, because border-box includes everything in the width
options.misconception: treats the whole width as content

options.text: 180px, removing only the padding
156px, after removing padding and border from both sides
196px, removing only the border

questions.explanation: Border-box makes the declared width include padding and border, so content width is 200 minus 40 padding minus 4 border, which is 156. Both padding and border reduce content space.
questions.hint: Subtract padding and border from both sides.

questions.topic: Collapsing two adjoining vertical margins
questions.learningObjective: Predict the resulting gap between two blocks
questions.stem: In a spreadsheet layout, two stacked blocks have top and bottom margins of 30px and 20px; what vertical gap appears between them?

options.text: 50px, the sum of both margins
options.misconception: adds adjoining margins instead of collapsing

options.text: 0px, because margins cancel each other
20px, the smaller of the two margins
30px, the larger of the two margins

questions.explanation: Adjoining vertical margins collapse to the larger value, so 30px and 20px produce a 30px gap. They do not add or cancel.
questions.hint: The larger margin wins when they collapse.

questions.topic: A percentage padding against the containing block
questions.learningObjective: Compute padding from a percentage value
questions.stem: A spreadsheet container is 400px wide and its child has padding 10%; what padding does each side receive?

options.text: 40px on each side, since 10% of 400 is 40
20px on each side, half of the horizontal value
10px on each side, treating percent as pixels
80px on each side, doubling for top and bottom
options.misconception: doubles the percentage for vertical sides

questions.explanation: Percentage padding resolves against the containing block's inline size, so 10% of 400px is 40px on every side. Vertical padding uses the same reference.
questions.hint: Percent padding resolves against container width.

questions.topic: Chaining a rem length into an em length
questions.learningObjective: Resolve a nested em against its parent
questions.stem: A spreadsheet's font-size is 16px root and a child sets font-size:2rem then padding:1em; a developer expects 16px padding. What is the error?

options.text: The developer assumes padding ignores font size entirely
options.misconception: thinks length units never depend on font size

options.text: The developer thinks rem resolves against the parent instead of root
The developer forgets em resolves against the element's own font size
The developer believes em and rem are identical units

questions.explanation: The child's font-size becomes 32px from 2rem, and 1em padding resolves against that 32px, yielding 32px rather than 16px. Em depends on the element's computed font size.
questions.hint: em uses the element's own font size.

questions.topic: A viewport unit against the window height
questions.learningObjective: Compute a length from a viewport unit
questions.stem: A spreadsheet preview pane is 800px tall and an element uses height:50vh; explain the computed height.

answer.exemplar: A vh unit equals one percent of the viewport height, so 50vh on an 800px tall window computes to 400px. The element therefore renders 400 pixels tall.

questions.explanation: Viewport units resolve against the viewport, not the parent, so 50vh is half the 800px window height. The result is 400px.
questions.hint: vh is one percent of viewport height.

questions.topic: A clickable div that a keyboard cannot use
questions.learningObjective: Identify the accessibility problem of a clickable div
questions.stem: A spreadsheet's toolbar uses a div with onclick to trigger save; why is this inaccessible to keyboard users?

options.text: The div's text is not selectable by screen readers
options.misconception: misattributes the issue to text selection

options.text: The div cannot receive mouse events in some browsers
options.misconception: confuses mouse support with keyboard support

options.text: The div is removed from the accessibility tree entirely
The div is not focusable and lacks keyboard activation by default

questions.explanation: A div is not focusable and has no default keyboard activation, so keyboard users cannot reach or trigger it. Using a button fixes focus and Enter/Space activation.
questions.hint: Divs are not focusable by default.

questions.topic: A fixed width that fits a laptop and not a phone
questions.learningObjective: Spot a non-responsive fixed width
questions.stem: A spreadsheet panel has width:900px; on a 390px phone screen what happens to the layout?

options.text: It becomes invisible below 900px
It shrinks automatically to fit the phone
It overflows horizontally and may cause scrolling
It wraps onto multiple lines
options.misconception: confuses block width with text wrapping

questions.explanation: A fixed 900px width exceeds a 390px viewport, so the panel overflows horizontally and can trigger horizontal scrolling. Fixed widths do not adapt.
questions.hint: Fixed widths do not adapt to small screens.

questions.topic: A full width row that overflows because of its padding
questions.learningObjective: Explain overflow from width plus padding
questions.stem: A spreadsheet row is width:100% with 20px horizontal padding under content-box; why does it overflow its container?

options.text: Padding is subtracted from the width automatically
The percentage width ignores padding entirely
options.misconception: thinks padding is excluded from total

options.text: The container shrinks to fit the row
The padding adds to the 100% width, exceeding the container

questions.explanation: Under content-box, width:100% sets only the content width, and padding adds on top, pushing the total past 100% of the container. Border-box would include padding in the 100%.
questions.hint: Padding sits outside the declared width in content-box.

questions.topic: Choosing padding to reach a target outer width
questions.learningObjective: Choose padding to hit a target outer width
questions.stem: A spreadsheet wants a 220px outer box with content-box width 200px and 5px border; a developer sets 10px padding per side. What is the error?

options.text: The developer used border-box math on a content-box element
The developer forgot padding adds on both sides
The developer ignored the border contribution
The developer set padding too small to matter

questions.explanation: With 10px padding on both sides, outer width is 200 + 20 + 10 = 230px, not 220px. To reach 220px, total horizontal padding plus border must equal 20px.
questions.hint: Padding applies to both sides.

questions.topic: Percentage padding then the outer width it produces
questions.learningObjective: Compute outer width from percentage padding
questions.stem: A spreadsheet card has width 300px, padding 5%, and 1px border under content-box; explain the outer width.

answer.exemplar: Five percent of 300px is 15px per side, so horizontal padding totals 30px and borders add 2px, giving an outer width of 332px.

questions.explanation: Percentage padding resolves against the 300px container width, yielding 15px per side. Adding content, padding, and border gives 332px total.
questions.hint: Resolve the percent against the container width.

questions.topic: Why adjoining vertical margins become one gap
questions.learningObjective: Explain margin collapse between siblings
questions.stem: In a spreadsheet, two adjacent sections each have 24px bottom and top margins; why is the gap 24px not 48px?

options.text: One margin is ignored because it is duplicate
The browser subtracts the smaller margin from the larger
Adjoining vertical margins collapse to the larger value
Margins only apply to the first element

questions.explanation: Vertical margins of adjacent blocks collapse into a single margin equal to the larger of the two, so 24px and 24px yield 24px. They do not sum.
questions.hint: Adjoining margins collapse, not add.

questions.topic: A label and the control it describes
questions.learningObjective: Associate a label with its input
questions.stem: In a spreadsheet's filter form, which markup correctly associates the text 'Amount' with its input?

options.text: <label id='amount'>Amount</label><input for='amount'>
options.misconception: swaps the for and id attributes

options.text: <label>Amount</label><input name='amount'>
options.misconception: relies on name instead of for/id pairing

options.text: Amount
options.misconception: uses a span with no label association

options.text: <label for='amount'>Amount</label><input id='amount'>

questions.explanation: A label associates with an input through matching for and id attributes. Name or span alone does not create that association.
questions.hint: Match the label's for to the input's id.

questions.topic: Where a required field is enforced
questions.learningObjective: Locate validation for a required field
questions.stem: A spreadsheet's form field has the required attribute; where is the emptiness check enforced?

options.text: Only on the server after the request arrives
In the browser before submission
In the CSS engine while rendering
In the database when the row is inserted
options.misconception: places validation too late in the flow

questions.explanation: The required attribute triggers built-in constraint validation in the browser before the form submits. Server checks may still be needed but are separate.
questions.hint: required is enforced by the browser.

questions.topic: Tabs and spaces in source and in a preserved listing
questions.learningObjective: Choose the element that preserves whitespace
questions.stem: A spreadsheet's code listing must show tabs and spaces exactly; a developer uses a normal div. What is the error?

options.text: CSS always preserves tabs in every element
The div cannot contain tab characters at all
options.misconception: thinks tabs are invalid in HTML

options.text: A normal div collapses whitespace, so tabs and spaces disappear
Tabs are converted to spaces by the parser

questions.explanation: Normal flow collapses whitespace runs, so a div will not preserve tabs and spaces. Use pre or white-space:pre to keep them visible.
questions.hint: Use pre or white-space:pre.

questions.topic: Why the initial box-sizing surprises people
questions.learningObjective: Explain why content-box surprises developers
questions.stem: A spreadsheet developer sets width:200px but measures 244px on screen and is surprised; explain why.

answer.exemplar: The initial box-sizing is content-box, so the declared width covers only content and padding plus border are added on top, making the rendered box wider than expected.

questions.explanation: Content-box counts only content in the width, so padding and border increase the total. Developers often expect the declared width to be the outer width.
questions.hint: Content-box excludes padding and border from width.

questions.topic: Which flex property works along the line and which across it
questions.learningObjective: Map flex properties to axes
questions.stem: In a spreadsheet's flex toolbar, which property distributes space along the main axis and which aligns across the cross axis?

options.text: order along the main axis, flex-basis across the cross axis
align-items along the main axis, justify-content across the cross axis
flex-grow along the main axis, flex-shrink across the cross axis
justify-content along the main axis, align-items across the cross axis

questions.explanation: justify-content distributes free space along the main axis, while align-items aligns items across the cross axis. Swapping them is a common error.
questions.hint: justify for main, align for cross.

questions.topic: What a media query changes and what it leaves alone
questions.learningObjective: State the scope of a media query
questions.stem: A spreadsheet's media query changes the sidebar width at 768px; what does it not change automatically?

options.text: The computed width of the sidebar
The DOM order and the markup structure
The color scheme applied to the page
The font size of the body text

questions.explanation: A media query only applies CSS rules conditionally; it does not alter the DOM or markup structure. Structure stays the same while styles adapt.
questions.hint: Media queries change styles, not markup.

questions.topic: Breaking a tie between equally specific rules
questions.learningObjective: Resolve a specificity tie with source order
questions.stem: Two equally specific rules in a spreadsheet theme set color to red and blue; which color wins?

options.text: The browser picks randomly between them
The first rule always wins regardless of order
The later rule in source order wins
Both colors are applied and blended

questions.explanation: When specificity is equal, the later declaration in source order wins. Earlier rules do not override later ones at the same specificity.
questions.hint: Later source order wins ties.

questions.topic: Dividing a grid container between three fractional tracks
questions.learningObjective: Compute grid track sizes from fr units
questions.stem: A spreadsheet grid uses 1fr 1fr 1fr on a 300px container; a developer expects each track to be 100px plus padding. What is the error?

options.text: The developer assumes grid ignores container width
options.misconception: thinks tracks size to content only

options.text: The developer thinks fr units include padding automatically
The developer believes fr units are percentages
The developer added padding to the fractional track size

questions.explanation: Fractional units divide the available space, so three 1fr tracks on 300px give 100px each before padding. Padding is added outside unless border-box is set.
questions.hint: fr divides available space, not padding.

questions.topic: A fixed track beside a fractional one
questions.learningObjective: Compute a fractional track beside a fixed track
questions.stem: A spreadsheet grid has columns 100px and 1fr on a 400px container; explain the second track's width.

answer.exemplar: The fixed track takes 100px first, leaving 300px for the fractional track, so the 1fr column renders 300px wide.

questions.explanation: Fixed tracks are subtracted from the container before fractional units divide the remainder. Thus 1fr gets 300px here.
questions.hint: Subtract fixed tracks before dividing fr.

questions.topic: Weighted shrinking along a flex line
questions.learningObjective: Predict flex shrink distribution
questions.stem: Two flex items on an overfull line have flex-shrink 1 and 2; which item shrinks more?

options.text: Both shrink by the same amount
The item with flex-shrink 2 shrinks more
The item with flex-shrink 1 shrinks more
Neither shrinks because the line is overfull

questions.explanation: Flex shrink distributes overflow proportionally to shrink factors, so the item with factor 2 shrinks twice as much as the one with factor 1. Equal shrinking would ignore the weights.
questions.hint: Higher shrink factor means more shrink.

questions.topic: Distributing free space with space-between
questions.learningObjective: Describe space-between distribution
questions.stem: A spreadsheet flex row uses justify-content:space-between with three items; where does the free space go?

options.text: All free space before the first item
options.misconception: imagines left alignment with trailing space

options.text: Equally on both outer ends only
Between the items, with none at the ends
The free space is discarded entirely

questions.explanation: space-between pushes items to the ends and places all free space between adjacent items, leaving no gap at the outer edges. It does not add end gaps.
questions.hint: Space goes between, not at ends.

questions.topic: Counting the elements a descendant selector reaches
questions.learningObjective: Count nodes matched by a descendant selector
questions.stem:
In markup
  • a
  • b
, how many elements does '.list span' match?

options.text: Zero, because span is not a direct child
Two, both li elements
options.misconception: matches the li instead of span

options.text: Three, all nodes in the list
One, the span inside the second li

questions.explanation: The descendant selector matches any span nested anywhere inside .list, which is just the one span. It does not require direct childhood.
questions.hint: Descendant means any depth.

questions.topic: Choosing the winning declaration among three rules
questions.learningObjective: Pick the highest-specificity declaration
questions.stem: Three rules target a spreadsheet cell with selectors .cell, #cell, and div.cell; which color declaration wins?

options.text: The .cell rule wins because class is most common
The #cell rule wins because id has highest specificity
The div.cell rule wins because it has two parts
options.misconception: counts parts instead of specificity weight

options.text: The first rule in source order wins

questions.explanation: Id selectors outweigh class and element selectors, so #cell wins regardless of source order. Counting parts or preferring common selectors is wrong.
questions.hint: Id beats class beats element.

questions.topic: Counting list items when an end tag is missing
questions.learningObjective: Predict parser behavior with a missing li end tag
questions.stem:
A spreadsheet list has
  • one
  • two
    • ; explain how many list items the parser creates.

answer.exemplar: The parser implicitly closes the first li when it encounters the second li start tag, so two separate list items are created despite the missing end tag.

questions.explanation: li end tags are optional; a new li start tag closes the previous one. Thus two items result even though only one end tag appears.
questions.hint: A new li closes the previous one.

questions.topic: Margins that stop collapsing inside a flex container
questions.learningObjective: State when margin collapse stops
questions.stem: In a spreadsheet flex column, do the vertical margins of child items collapse?

options.text: Only the first and last margins collapse
Yes, they collapse exactly like block siblings
No, flex containers establish a new formatting context that prevents collapse
Margins are removed entirely inside flex

questions.explanation: Flex formatting contexts prevent margin collapse between flex items, so each margin applies fully. They do not collapse like normal block siblings.
questions.hint: Flex prevents margin collapse.

questions.topic: Hiding an element without removing its space
questions.learningObjective: Choose the property that hides but keeps space
questions.stem: A spreadsheet wants a placeholder to vanish visually but keep its layout space; which CSS achieves that?

options.text: position:absolute keeps the space while hiding
display:none keeps the space while hiding the element
opacity:0 removes the space while hiding the element
visibility:hidden keeps the space while hiding the element

questions.explanation: visibility:hidden hides the element but preserves its box in layout, while display:none removes it from layout entirely. Opacity keeps space but the element remains interactive.
questions.hint: visibility:hidden keeps layout space.

questions.topic: Working out the shared space behind a fractional track
questions.learningObjective: Compute space shared by fr tracks
questions.stem: A spreadsheet grid has columns 1fr 2fr on a 300px container; what widths result?

options.text: 150px and 150px, splitting equally
100px and 200px, splitting three parts
75px and 225px, misweighting the ratio
300px and 0px, giving all space to the first

questions.explanation: The fr values sum to 3 parts, so 1fr gets one-third (100px) and 2fr gets two-thirds (200px) of the 300px container. The ratio must be respected.
questions.hint: Divide by the sum of fr values.

questions.topic: An item that cannot shrink on an overfull line
questions.learningObjective: Prevent an item from shrinking
questions.stem: A spreadsheet flex item must keep its width on an overfull line; a developer sets flex-shrink:0. What is verified?

options.text: The item grows to fill remaining space
The item disappears from the line
The item will not shrink below its flex basis
The item wraps to the next line automatically

questions.explanation: flex-shrink:0 disables shrinking, so the item holds its flex basis even when the line is overfull, causing overflow rather than shrink. It does not remove or wrap the item.
questions.hint: Zero shrink means no shrinking.

questions.topic: Why a declared width is not the width on screen
questions.learningObjective: Explain why declared width differs from rendered width
questions.stem: A spreadsheet developer declares width:200px but the box measures 244px; explain the discrepancy.

answer.exemplar: The declared width applies to content only under the default content-box sizing, while padding and border add extra pixels, so the rendered box is wider than declared.

questions.explanation: Content-box excludes padding and border from width, causing the rendered box to exceed the declaration. Switching to border-box makes the declared width the outer width.
questions.hint: Padding and border add to content width.

questions.topic: The order from a document to painted boxes
questions.learningObjective: Order the stages from markup to paint
questions.stem: In a spreadsheet's browser pipeline, what is the order from HTML to painted pixels?

options.text: Compute styles, parse HTML, layout, paint
Paint first, then layout, then parse HTML
Build DOM, paint, then compute styles
Parse HTML, build DOM, compute styles, layout, paint

questions.explanation: The browser parses HTML into a DOM, computes styles, performs layout, and then paints. Reversing or skipping stages misrepresents the pipeline.
questions.hint: Parse, style, layout, paint.

questions.topic: The document as a tree rather than a typed sequence
questions.learningObjective: Identify sibling relationships in the DOM
questions.stem:
In markup

Title

note

total

, how many element siblings does the h2 have?

options.text: One, only the first p
options.misconception: counts only the immediately following sibling

options.text: Two, the two p elements
Three, including the section itself
options.misconception: includes the parent as a sibling

options.text: Zero, because h2 has no siblings

questions.explanation: The h2's element siblings are the two p elements that share the same parent section. The section is the parent, not a sibling.
questions.hint: Siblings share a parent.

questions.topic: A block element written inside a paragraph
questions.learningObjective: Predict paragraph splitting with a block child
questions.stem: A spreadsheet note places a table inside a p; what structure results after parsing?

options.text: The paragraph and table are both discarded
The table stays nested inside the paragraph
The paragraph splits around the table as siblings
The table is converted into a span

questions.explanation: A paragraph cannot contain a table, so the parser closes the p before the table and may open a new p after it. The table becomes a sibling.
questions.hint: Block content ends the paragraph.

questions.topic: Display decides block or inline, not the tag name
questions.learningObjective: Predict rendering from a display override
questions.stem: A spreadsheet sets span { display:block } and a teammate says it still flows inline. What is the error?

options.text: The teammate confuses span with div rendering
The teammate thinks span cannot be block ever
The teammate believes CSS does not apply to spans
The teammate ignores the display override that makes it block

questions.explanation: Display:block overrides the span's default inline behavior, so it generates a block box. The tag name does not lock the display value.
questions.hint: display overrides the tag default.

questions.topic: Choosing an element for what it means rather than how it looks
questions.learningObjective: Explain why semantic markup matters
questions.stem: A spreadsheet app uses a styled div instead of a nav for its menu; explain the downside.

answer.exemplar: A styled div lacks the navigation landmark role, so assistive technology and search tools cannot identify the menu as navigation, reducing accessibility and machine readability.

questions.explanation: Semantic elements expose roles to assistive technology and tools. A styled div provides no landmark semantics, harming accessibility.
questions.hint: Semantic elements expose roles.

questions.topic: What a heading outline with a skipped level claims
questions.learningObjective: Describe outline impact of skipping levels
questions.stem: A spreadsheet report uses h1 then h3; what does the outline imply?

options.text: The h3 is treated as a sibling of the h1
An implied h2 exists between them
The outline is discarded entirely
The h3 becomes an h2 automatically

questions.explanation: Skipping from h1 to h3 implies a missing h2 parent, so the h3 nests under an implied heading. The outline still parses but represents that gap.
questions.hint: A gap implies a missing parent.

questions.topic: Heading levels are structure rather than size
questions.learningObjective: Choose the correct heading by structure
questions.stem: A spreadsheet section is nested under an h2; which heading level should its title use?

options.text: h2, to match the parent size
h1, because it is the most important section
h3, because it is one level deeper than h2
h4, skipping a level for emphasis

questions.explanation: Headings reflect document structure, so a section nested under an h2 should use h3. Importance or size does not determine the level.
questions.hint: Nesting determines the level.

questions.topic: What a form actually submits
questions.learningObjective: Identify submitted values with defaults
questions.stem: A spreadsheet form field has name='qty' and value='5' but is disabled; is qty submitted?

options.text: No, because disabled removes the name
Yes, with value 5
Yes, but with an empty value
No, disabled controls are not successful

questions.explanation: Disabled controls are not successful and are excluded from submission. Only enabled controls with names contribute.
questions.hint: Disabled controls are skipped.

questions.topic: Collapsing a run of white space in ordinary text
questions.learningObjective: Predict whitespace collapse with newlines
questions.stem: A spreadsheet note has a newline between two sentences; a reviewer expects a line break. What is the error?

options.text: Newlines always render as line breaks
Newlines collapse to a single space in normal flow
Only tabs collapse, not newlines
Newlines are removed entirely
options.misconception: thinks newlines vanish instead of collapsing

questions.explanation: In normal flow, newlines collapse to a single space along with other whitespace. A line break requires br or pre formatting.
questions.hint: Newlines collapse to one space.

questions.topic: The outer width under the initial box-sizing
questions.learningObjective: Compute outer width with padding and border
questions.stem: A spreadsheet box has width 150px, padding 10px, border 5px under content-box; explain the outer width.

answer.exemplar: Under content-box the 150px covers content only, so outer width is 150 plus 20 padding plus 10 border, totaling 180 pixels.

questions.explanation: Content-box width excludes padding and border, which are added to get the outer width. Here that totals 180px.
questions.hint: Add padding and border to content width.

questions.topic: The content width under border-box sizing
questions.learningObjective: Compute content width with border-box
questions.stem: A spreadsheet panel uses border-box with width 180px, padding 12px, border 3px; what is the content width?

options.text: 168px, removing only padding
180px, because border-box keeps content separate
options.misconception: thinks border-box excludes content from width

options.text: 150px, after removing padding and border both sides
174px, removing only border

questions.explanation: Border-box includes padding and border in the declared width, so content width is 180 minus 24 padding minus 6 border, which is 150. Both must be subtracted.
questions.hint: Subtract padding and border both sides.

questions.topic: Collapsing two adjoining vertical margins
questions.learningObjective: Predict collapsed margin with unequal values
questions.stem: Two spreadsheet sections have margins 12px and 40px; what gap appears between them?

options.text: 28px, the difference of the margins
52px, the sum of both margins
12px, the smaller margin
40px, the larger margin

questions.explanation: Adjoining vertical margins collapse to the larger value, so 12px and 40px produce a 40px gap. They neither add nor subtract.
questions.hint: The larger margin wins.

questions.topic: A percentage padding against the containing block
questions.learningObjective: Compute percentage padding on all sides
questions.stem: A spreadsheet container is 500px wide and its child has padding 8%; what is the padding per side?

options.text: 8px per side, treating percent as pixels
40px per side, 8% of 500
20px per side, half the horizontal value
80px per side, doubling for vertical

questions.explanation: Percentage padding resolves against the containing block's inline size, so 8% of 500px is 40px on every side. Vertical padding uses the same reference.
questions.hint: Percent resolves against container width.

questions.topic: Chaining a rem length into an em length
questions.learningObjective: Resolve em after a rem font size
questions.stem: Root font-size is 16px, a box sets font-size:1.5rem then margin:2em; a developer expects 32px margin. What is the error?

options.text: The developer assumes margin ignores font size
The developer thinks rem resolves against the parent
The developer forgets em resolves against the 24px font size, giving 48px
The developer believes em equals rem always

questions.explanation: 1.5rem makes the font size 24px, and 2em resolves against that, yielding 48px rather than 32px. Em depends on the element's own font size.
questions.hint: em uses the element's font size.

questions.topic: A viewport unit against the window height
questions.learningObjective: Compute a vh length
questions.stem: A spreadsheet preview window is 600px tall and an element uses height:25vh; explain the computed height.

answer.exemplar: One vh equals one percent of the viewport height, so 25vh on a 600px window computes to 150px. The element renders 150 pixels tall.

questions.explanation: Viewport units resolve against the viewport height, so 25vh is a quarter of 600px. The result is 150px.
questions.hint: vh is one percent of viewport height.

questions.topic: A clickable div that a keyboard cannot use
questions.learningObjective: Identify missing keyboard support
questions.stem: A spreadsheet uses a div with tabindex and onclick for deletion; what remains missing for keyboard users?

options.text: Screen reader announcement only
Mouse click support
Focus styling only
options.misconception: thinks focus style is the only gap

options.text: Keyboard activation on Enter or Space

questions.explanation: tabindex makes the div focusable but does not add keyboard activation, so Enter or Space does nothing. A button provides both focus and activation.
questions.hint: Focusability alone is not enough.

questions.topic: A fixed width that fits a laptop and not a phone
questions.learningObjective: Recommend a responsive alternative
questions.stem: A spreadsheet panel uses width:1024px; on a 414px phone, which approach fixes the overflow?

options.text: Increase the fixed width to 1200px
Use max-width with a relative width instead of a fixed width
Set overflow:hidden on the body
Remove all padding from the panel

questions.explanation: Replacing the fixed width with a relative width and max-width lets the panel adapt to small screens. Larger fixed widths or clipping do not solve responsiveness.
questions.hint: Use relative widths with max-width.

questions.topic: A full width row that overflows because of its padding
questions.learningObjective: Fix overflow from width plus padding
questions.stem: A spreadsheet row is width:100% with 16px horizontal padding under content-box; how do you prevent overflow?

options.text: Remove the padding entirely
Set width to 100% plus the padding value
Switch to border-box so padding is included in the width
Set overflow:scroll on the container

questions.explanation: Border-box includes padding in the declared width, so width:100% accounts for padding and prevents overflow. Removing padding or scrolling avoids the real fix.
questions.hint: Use border-box for width plus padding.

questions.topic: Choosing padding to reach a target outer width
questions.learningObjective: Choose padding for a target outer width
questions.stem: A spreadsheet wants 210px outer width with content-box width 200px and no border; a developer sets 10px padding total. What is the error?

options.text: The developer set padding too large
The developer forgot the border contribution
options.misconception: invents a border that does not exist

options.text: The developer used border-box math
Padding must be split across both sides, so 10px total is not 10px each

questions.explanation: 10px total horizontal padding means 5px per side, giving 210px outer width. Setting 10px per side would yield 220px. The total must be split across sides.
questions.hint: Split padding across both sides.

questions.topic: Percentage padding then the outer width it produces
questions.learningObjective: Compute outer width from percent padding
questions.stem: A spreadsheet card has width 250px, padding 4%, and 2px border under content-box; explain the outer width.

answer.exemplar: Four percent of 250px is 10px per side, so horizontal padding totals 20px and borders add 4px, producing an outer width of 274px.

questions.explanation: Percentage padding resolves against the 250px width, giving 10px per side. Adding content, padding, and border yields 274px.
questions.hint: Resolve percent against container width.

questions.topic: Why adjoining vertical margins become one gap
questions.learningObjective: Explain margin collapse to a colleague
questions.stem: A spreadsheet has two stacked blocks with 18px and 26px margins; why is the gap 26px?

options.text: The smaller margin is subtracted from the larger
Adjoining vertical margins collapse to the larger value
The margins add to 44px then halve
Only the first margin applies

questions.explanation: Vertical margins of adjacent blocks collapse to the larger value, so 18px and 26px yield 26px. They do not add, subtract, or average.
questions.hint: The larger margin wins.
